taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Maakoro-street (Bori Metropolis). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 168 | 1.71 | 1.71
2 | 484 | 7.45 | 9.16
3 | 255 | 15.3 | 24.4
4 | 1109 | 25 | 49.4
5 | 807 | 74.2 | 124
6 | 8895 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as Q-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: Maakoro-street (Bori Metropolis)
Curve type: KHKH (re-derived from the resistivity sequence: layers 1‑2‑3 = K, 2‑3‑4 = H, 3‑4‑5 = K, 4‑5‑6 = H — note this corrects the file’s “Q‑type” label, which does not match the resistivity progression)
Aquifer depth: 24.4 m – 124 m (the resistive sand sequence of layers 4 and 5, sandwiched between lower‑resistivity clayey layers)

Recommendation: Target the screened interval within the 24.4–124 m depth range, where the resistive sand units (1109 Ω·m and 807 Ω·m) indicate the most permeable, water‑bearing horizon; set casing through the overlying clay/sandy‑clay sequence (0–24.4 m) to prevent cross‑contamination and borehole collapse, and confirm lithology with cuttings/geophysical logging during drilling since the resistivity pattern deviates from the originally filed Q‑type interpretation.
